h: Co-President Adjourns Meeting Early, Nobody Leaves, She Is Forced To Leave Her Own Meeting
b: The agenda concluded at 8:56 PM. Sources confirm she said the words 'that's everything, go home,' collected her laptop, and walked out. Nobody followed her.

Twenty-two members remained in JFF for another forty minutes, arguing about a chart on a deck that is not due until Thursday. At no point did anyone acknowledge that the meeting had ended. One member ordered food to the building.
At press time she had returned for her water bottle, found the room still full, made brief eye contact with the group, and left again without comment.

h: Co-Presidents Have Not Publicly Disagreed Once All Semester, Club Growing Uneasy
b: Members have documented four occasions on which both co-presidents began the same sentence, at the same time, at the same volume. A freshman who asked which one he should email was told 'either,' by both of them, simultaneously.

One sophomore attempted to start a rumor that they had fought over a room booking. The rumor died within an hour because, in her words, nobody could picture it. A second member described the situation as 'genuinely lovely and also something I think about before I fall asleep.'

At press time an anonymous source had proposed asking them a divisive question in public purely to see what would happen, and had been talked down by three separate people who said they were not ready for that.

h: VP Of Engagements Knows Client's Dog's Name, Client Knows His Midterm Schedule
b: The engagement began in September as a standard ten week scope. It is now a relationship that both parties are, by all accounts, unable to keep at a professional distance.

He knows the dog. He knows the dog is a rescue and he knows what she is like around the mail carrier. She, in turn, moved a stakeholder call because she remembered he had a midterm, without being told, correctly, on the right day.
At press time the deliverable had been submitted a week early, and the Post has been asked not to print what the client wrote at the bottom of the thank-you email.

h: Man Attends Fifteen Minute Coffee Chat, Leaves Ninety Minutes Later Having Changed His Minor
b: He had one question about the interview process. Witnesses at the adjacent table report that by minute forty they were discussing his father, and by minute seventy she was drawing three boxes and an arrow on a napkin.

He did not get his question answered. He has not noticed. Two days later he filed the paperwork to switch, citing the napkin, which he was carrying, and which he has since had laminated at the FedEx on Figueroa.
At press time he had booked a second coffee chat, telling friends he wanted to 'run one more thing by her,' and had cleared the entire afternoon.

h: Team Now Runs A 'Vishal Check' Before Every Presentation, Has Not Told Vishal
b: The practice began after a working session in October, when a single question about what the client actually needed reduced six weeks of market entry strategy to a supporting slide. Someone had printed that deck. There were tabs in it.

The procedure is now standard. Before any deliverable goes out, a team member is designated to sit in a chair and ask the question in his voice, and the group answers it honestly, in private, where it is survivable. Multiple project teams have adopted it independently.

At press time he remained unaware that a recurring meeting on four calendars is named after him, and the printed copies of the original deck were still in a drawer in JFF, because nobody has been able to recycle them.

h: One Font Change Spreads To Four Resumes, A Midterm, And One Wedding Invitation
b: The original edit affected forty-one slides and nothing else. Not one figure, recommendation, or title was touched. A team member, convinced something more must have changed, opened both versions side by side and compared them for eleven minutes before giving up.

The font has since been observed on four member resumes, a marketing midterm submitted in the business school, a personal website, and the save-the-date for a cousin's wedding in Sacramento. None of these people asked her. Most of them cannot name it.
At press time the Post had confirmed that she does not know about the wedding.

h: VP Of Finance Institutes Snack Policy, Compliance Voluntary, Compliance Total
b: The policy followed the discovery of forty dollars in a line item that members describe as 'the one nobody was in charge of.' It had been sitting there since spring. It is now the most consequential forty dollars in the organization.

The rules are unenforced and universally obeyed. One member declined to comment on the arrangement while holding two granola bars, with a third visible in his jacket pocket, which he did not attempt to explain.
At press time she had projected the fund through December, the room had erupted, and someone in the back had shouted a larger number at her, which she is reportedly considering.

h: VP Of Events Maintains Spreadsheet Of Every Room On Campus, Including Which Ones Have Outlets
b: The file has eleven columns. Capacity, projector, whether the door locks behind you, whether the third-floor ones are worth it, and a freeform notes field that members describe as 'where the real information is.'

It is the reason the last general meeting occurred in the room printed on the invitation, at the time printed on the invitation, with more chairs than people and a door that was already unlocked. One attendee, finding the event underway in the advertised location, briefly assumed he was in the wrong place.
At press time two other USC organizations had requested access to the file and been politely declined.

h: First-Year Mumbles Something Into His Hoodie, PM Stops Entire Room And Makes Him Say It Again
b: The comment was made at low volume and was not intended to be heard. Sources report she raised a hand, stopped a conversation that eight people were already inside of, and asked him to repeat it.

He repeated it. There was a pause. It is now the recommendation, it is on slide nine, and his name is in the speaker notes, where it has remained despite two separate requests from him to have it removed.
At press time he had spoken unprompted in three consecutive meetings, a development his roommate has described as 'honestly kind of a lot to be around.'

h: PM Reads Entire Appendix, Discovers Slide Nobody On The Team Will Admit To Making
b: The appendix ran nineteen slides, assembled over four weeks by five people, none of whom had read it end to end. She opened it on a Tuesday. She did not resurface until Wednesday.

Her findings included two contradictions, a chart of unknown origin, and slide fifty-two, which no member of the team recognizes, claims, or can account for. Version history shows it was created at 3:14 AM by an account that all five insist was not theirs.
At press time slide fifty-two had been promoted to the main body of the deck, where it is the single strongest slide in the presentation, and where it is now attributed to the team.

h: PM Opens Google Doc, Finds Eleven Anonymous Animals Inside, Greets Each By Name
b: The document had been shared nineteen minutes earlier. By the time he opened it, eleven anonymous animals were moving through the outline, three of them editing the same sentence at once.

He did not ask anyone to identify themselves. Sources report he simply began addressing them individually in the comments, correctly, on the basis of cursor behavior alone. Multiple members confirmed they were 'genuinely a little unsettled' and also 'weirdly touched.'
At press time the outline was finished, and nobody had worked up the nerve to ask how he knew which one was the Anonymous Capybara.

h: PM Asks Team If They Are Asleep, Four Members Lie, She Knows
b: The messages went out between 12:40 and 1:15 AM, one to each member, all of them some version of the question 'are you still up.' Four replied that they were not.

One of them replied 'no' in nine seconds. One replied 'asleep' from a laptop while editing slide twenty-two, which she was watching him edit. One sent a thumbs up, which sources agree is not a response a sleeping person produces. All four were told to go to bed. All four went to bed.
At press time the team had begun coordinating their lies in a separate group chat, and she had been added to it by mistake, and had said nothing about it for six days.

h: Faculty Advisor Asks One Eight-Word Question, Six Students Rethink Their Majors, He Was Being Nice
b: It was not a challenge. It was not a correction. Witnesses are unanimous that the tone was warm, curious, and completely devastating, and that he appeared to have no idea what he had done.

The room went quiet for a period estimated at between four and nine seconds. One student later said she had spent two years constructing an answer to a question that had never once been asked out loud in front of her.
At press time the workstream had been rebuilt from scratch, was substantially better, and no member of the team had been able to bring themselves to tell him he caused it.
